subject: TypeScript from first principles, to build an AI agent harness

learner.background: Programmer, thinks in Python. New to JavaScript.
owned_priors: Python object model and duck typing
Python type hints: Optional, Union, TypeVar, Protocol
asyncio: async def, await, async for
Blocking I/O as the default mental model
learner.end_goal: A working CLI agent: typed tool registry, streaming provider call, async-generator event loop, file and bash tools. pi's spine, written from scratch.

resources.codebase: pi/ — packages/agent (the spine), packages/ai (provider layer + event unions)
resources.known_gaps: All four transcripts have ZERO coverage of await/yield/generator/iterator. Rungs 0 and 5 are grounded in primary docs (MDN, TS handbook) and pi's own source instead.

cruxes.title: The machine underneath
cruxes.hook: JavaScript has one thread and it must never stop. So "not yet" has to become a value you can hold.
cruxes.owns: Python's blocking mental model, and asyncio as the exception that proves the rule
cruxes.payoff: The Promise, derived rather than defined. And the seed of the whole harness: an LLM response is the ultimate not-yet.

cruxes.title: A type is a set of values
cruxes.hook: Everything TypeScript does is set membership. `extends` means ⊆. Once you read it that way, nothing in the language is magic again.
cruxes.owns: Python duck typing; the intuition that shape decides what works
cruxes.payoff: Structural typing, `never` as ∅, `unknown` as 𝕌, and erasure — why TS types cannot be inspected at runtime the way Python's can.
cruxes.verified: All 10 type-algebra claims in this lesson checked against tsc 5.9.3 --strict via @ts-expect-error harness. Includes the excess-property (freshness) exception.

cruxes.title: Narrowing is set arithmetic
cruxes.hook: A union is a set union. Narrowing shrinks it. Exhaustiveness works because what's left over is the empty set.
cruxes.payoff: Discriminated unions — how every message and every stream event in pi is modelled. `AssistantMessageEvent` has 12 members (types.ts:523-539) and the loop switches on all of them.

cruxes.title: Generics: functions from types to types
cruxes.hook: You already write functions over values. These are functions over sets — and constraints are just ⊆ again.
cruxes.payoff: `Tool<TSchema>` — a tool whose argument type is a parameter.

cruxes.title: Types that compute
cruxes.hook: Conditional types are pattern matching on sets. `infer` is destructuring. The type system is a language, and you can run it.
cruxes.payoff: `Static<T>` — deriving a tool's argument type from its JSON schema. Your Pydantic moment, except it costs nothing at runtime. Also `Extract<AssistantMessage["content"][number], {type:"toolCall"}>` from pi's types.ts.

cruxes.title: Async as a stream
cruxes.hook: A Promise is one not-yet. An async generator is a sequence of them. An LLM response is exactly that.
cruxes.payoff: `for await (const event of response)` — the line the entire harness is built around.

cruxes.title: BUILD: the harness spine
cruxes.hook: Every rung so far was load-bearing for one while-loop. Now write it.
cruxes.payoff: A typed tool registry, a streaming provider call, the agent loop, tool execution. ~300 lines you can defend line by line.

cruxes.title: BUILD: the CLI agent
cruxes.hook: Make it a thing you actually use.
cruxes.payoff: stdin/stdout, streaming render, read/write/bash tools. A working coding agent.
